questions.q: She gave me some useful ___ about the job.
questions.why: 'Information' is uncountable, so it has no plural and takes no 'a/an'.

questions.q: Can I ask you for ___?
questions.why: 'Advice' is uncountable; use 'some advice', never 'an advice' or 'advices'.

questions.q: We bought new ___ for the living room.
questions.why: 'Furniture' is uncountable and never takes a plural -s.

questions.q: The ___ on TV last night ___ shocking.
questions.why: 'News' is uncountable and singular, so it takes 'was', not 'were'.

questions.q: How ___ money do you have on you?
questions.why: Use 'much' with uncountable nouns like 'money'; 'many' is for countables.

questions.q: There are too ___ chairs in this room.
questions.why: Use 'many' with countable plural nouns like 'chairs'.

questions.q: He did a lot of ___ on the project.
questions.why: 'Work' meaning effort/labour is uncountable and takes no plural -s.

questions.q: Let me give you a ___ of advice.
questions.why: We count uncountables with 'a piece of', e.g. 'a piece of advice'.

questions.q: I packed only one bag, so I don't have much ___.
questions.why: 'Luggage' is uncountable; for one item say 'a piece of luggage'.

questions.q: Could you buy some ___ from the bakery?
questions.why: 'Bread' is uncountable; to count it use 'a loaf of bread' or 'a slice of bread'.

questions.q: I'd like two ___ of bread, please.
questions.why: We make 'bread' countable with 'loaves'; note the irregular plural 'loaves'.

questions.q: How ___ luggage are you taking on the trip?
questions.why: 'Luggage' is uncountable, so we ask 'how much', not 'how many'.

questions.q: This ___ very interesting; I learned a lot.
questions.why: 'Information' is uncountable and singular, so it takes 'is'.

questions.q: She has three ___ of furniture to move.
questions.why: Count uncountables with 'pieces of', e.g. 'three pieces of furniture'.

questions.q: There ___ a lot of news today.
questions.why: 'News' is singular uncountable, so it takes singular 'was'.

questions.q: I need a few ___ before I decide.
questions.why: Use 'pieces of information' to count the uncountable noun 'information'.

questions.q: How ___ pieces of luggage do you have?
questions.why: 'Pieces' is countable, so use 'many' even though luggage itself is uncountable.

questions.q: My ___ great advice when I started.
questions.why: 'Advice' is uncountable, so no article is needed before it here.

questions.q: We don't have ___ furniture in the office.
questions.why: 'Furniture' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negatives, not 'many'.

questions.q: He earns a lot of ___ as an engineer.
questions.why: 'Money' is uncountable and takes no plural -s in everyday English.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She gave me a useful piece of ___ about studying.' (uncountable noun)
questions.why: 'Advice' is uncountable; count it with 'a piece of advice'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'The news ___ (be, present simple) on at six o'clock.'
questions.why: 'News' is singular uncountable, so the verb is 'is'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'How ___ money did the trip cost?' (much/many)
questions.why: 'Money' is uncountable, so we ask 'how much'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I bought two ___ of bread.' (plural of loaf)
questions.why: To count 'bread' we say 'loaves'; the irregular plural is 'loaves'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'There is too ___ furniture in this small flat.' (much/many)
questions.why: 'Furniture' is uncountable, so use 'much'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Can you give me some ___?' (uncountable noun meaning facts/details)
questions.why: 'Information' is uncountable; never write 'informations' or 'an information'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'He took only one ___ of luggage.' (counting word)
questions.why: Count uncountable 'luggage' with 'a piece of luggage'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'How ___ chairs do we need?' (much/many)
questions.why: 'Chairs' is countable plural, so use 'many'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I have a lot of ___ to do this weekend.' (uncountable noun meaning tasks/labour)
questions.why: 'Work' is uncountable; say 'a lot of work', not 'works'.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She gave me three pieces of ___ about my essay.' (uncountable)
questions.why: 'Advice' stays singular even after 'pieces of'; never 'advices'.
